questions.q: English ___ all over the world.
questions.why: Present simple passive uses 'is/are + past participle'.

questions.q: These cars ___ in Japan.
questions.why: A plural subject takes 'are + past participle' in the present passive.

questions.q: The bridge ___ in 1932.
questions.why: Past simple passive uses 'was/were + past participle'.

questions.q: The letters ___ yesterday.
questions.why: A plural subject in the past passive takes 'were + past participle'.

questions.q: My wallet ___ on the bus this morning.
questions.why: Past simple passive needs the past participle 'stolen', not 'stole'.

questions.q: The report ___ already ___.
questions.why: Present perfect passive uses 'has/have been + past participle'.

questions.q: Three suspects ___ by the police.
questions.why: Present perfect passive with a plural subject uses 'have been + past participle'.

questions.q: The new stadium ___ next year.
questions.why: Future passive uses 'will be + past participle'.

questions.q: The results ___ tomorrow.
questions.why: Future simple passive is formed with 'will be + past participle'.

questions.q: This form must ___ in black ink.
questions.why: Modal passive uses 'modal + be + past participle'.

questions.q: The work can ___ by Friday.
questions.why: After a modal, the passive is 'be + past participle'.

questions.q: Seat belts must ___ at all times.
questions.why: 'Must' + passive requires 'be + past participle' ('worn').

questions.q: The painting was created ___ a famous artist.
questions.why: The agent that performs the action is introduced with 'by'.

questions.q: The cake was cut ___ a sharp knife.
questions.why: Use 'with' for the instrument or tool, but 'by' for the doer.

questions.q: 'America was discovered ___ Columbus.'
questions.why: The by-agent names who performed the passive action.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct passive voice?
questions.why: Passive needs 'be' plus the past participle 'broken'.

questions.q: The thief ___ while he was climbing the fence.
questions.why: Get-passive uses 'get + past participle', common in informal speech.

questions.q: She ___ in the accident, luckily not seriously.
questions.why: Get-passive ('get injured') often describes unexpected events.

questions.q: Why is the passive often used in scientific writing?
options: To focus on the process, not the doer
questions.answer: To focus on the process, not the doer
questions.why: The passive is preferred when the action matters more than the agent.

questions.q: The road ___ at the moment, so take a detour.
questions.why: Present continuous passive uses 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.q: When the guests arrived, dinner ___.
questions.why: Past continuous passive uses 'was/were being + past participle'.

questions.q: The package ___ by the time I got home.
questions.why: Past perfect passive uses 'had been + past participle'.

questions.q: All visitors ___ to sign in at reception.
questions.why: Present simple passive with a plural subject uses 'are + past participle'.

questions.q: This problem should ___ immediately.
questions.why: Modal passive: 'should + be + past participle'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The house ___ (clean) every week.'
questions.why: Present simple passive uses 'is + past participle' for a singular subject.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The phone ___ (invent) by Alexander Bell.' (past)
questions.why: Past simple passive uses 'was + past participle'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'A new vaccine ___ (develop) recently.' (present perfect)
questions.why: Present perfect passive uses 'has been + past participle'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The winners ___ (announce) next week.' (future)
questions.why: Future passive uses 'will be + past participle'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'This door must ___ (keep) locked.' (modal)
questions.why: Modal passive uses 'modal + be + past participle'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'He ___ (get) promoted last month.' (get-passive, past)
questions.why: Get-passive in the past uses 'got + past participle'.
